title: OrthoHealth private deploy sizing and upgrade notes
content:
Audience: Solutions + Infra + OrthoHealth infra lead (initial scoping).
Status: working draft, not shared externally. Heavy TODOs and open questions inline.

High-level ask: produce a customer-ready private deployment plan for OrthoHealth (PHI environment, VPC peering to their DMZ, on-prem rack option). Provide recommended sizing, Terraform module notes for customer-managed infra, and a Stepwise upgrade plan (minor -> major) with rollbacks.

1) Summary recommendation (short)
- Deploy as private VPC-connected cluster in OrthoHealth Azure region (primary on-prem option later). Start with a 3-node Dedicated serving cluster backed by 4x A10 / or 2x A100 per node depending on model family. Use Redwood Private control plane in their VPC (managed) with HSM/KMS integration.
- Reserve burst capacity via dedicated-gpu-pool with autoscale set to 0-2 extra nodes for peak windows.
- Use our Terraform modules for inventory, networking, k8s resources, and monitoring; remote state stored in their secure blob store.

2) Assumptions (explicit)
- Target models: mixture of Llama2-70B and a distilled 13B variant for latency-critical endpoints.
- Peak traffic: 120 concurrent user sessions generating ~45 requests/sec, average 80 tokens/request, peak token rate ~3600 tps.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 350ms for short prompts (<512 tokens).
- Data residency: PHI data must remain in customer VPC/subnets. No outbound model telemetry without whitelisting.
- Customer can provide: VLAN-level network access, BGP advertised public IPs (for managed control plane), and HSM-backed KMS for keys.

3) Sizing rationale (detailed)
- Serving nodes: baseline 3 nodes. Each node: 2x A100 80GB (if available) or 4x A10 40GB alternative. Reason: Llama2-70B demands >40GB per model shard; A100 80GB allows a single-shard serving with simpler placement and better KV cache headroom.
- CPU: 48 vCPU per node to absorb preprocess, batching threads, and background housekeeping.
- RAM: 768GB host RAM to hold model working set and meta caches.
- Local storage: 4 x 4TB NVMe per node in RAID0 for fastest model load and KV cache. Persistent volumes: Ceph/Rook recommended for stateful artifacts (model weights can be on local NVMe and pulled by init).
- Network: 25Gbps NICs per node, RDMA if available for cross-node KV sync (recommended). Expect <1ms intra-rack latency.
- Caching: Prefix cache sized at ~256GB across cluster to cover hot prompt prefixes.
- Batching: target dynamic batching up to 32 tokens per batch at peak; throughput estimates assume average sequence length 80.

4) Capacity math (back-of-envelope)
- With 3 nodes each serving effectively 1.5 model instances (shard+replica), expect sustained throughput ~3k tokens/sec per A100-80GB under our runtime optimizations. So cluster baseline ~9k tps. Peak requirement headroom target = 2x traffic = 7.2k tps -> satisfies with buffer.
- Memory/KV: allocate 30% of host RAM to KV and embedding caches.

5) Network and security requirements (customer-facing checklist)
- Private subnets for serving nodes (no public internet egress).
- Control-plane connectivity: outbound TLS to Redwood control plane endpoints over whitelisted IPs (or use private link).
- KMS/HSM: support for external HSM or Azure KeyVault with HSM-backed keys; provide service principal for Redwood operator.
- Logging: forward audit logs to their SIEM (splunk/elastic) via TLS collector.
- Bastion for admin access; zero-trust recommended (no direct SSH from internet).

6) Terraform module notes (dev-facing)
- Modules to use: rwinfra/vpc, rwinfra/k8s-cluster, rwinfra/gpu-node-pool, rwinfra/kv-cache, rwinfra/monitoring.
- Required variables: cluster_name, region, subnet_ids (list), k8s_version, gpu_type, desired_gpu_count, storage_class_name, kms_key_id, remote_state_backend.
- Remote state: customer-managed blob (Azure Storage Account with RBAC). State encryption at rest required.
- Module behavior: gpu-node-pool module will create node-pool autoscaling groups and attach node labels used by scheduler. Add preemptible instance flag (default false) -- we recommend off for PHI.
- Feature flags: enable_prepull_images (boolean), enable_nvme_local_pv (boolean).
- Secrets: avoid storing keys in tfvars. Use key vault references and pass via k8s sealed secrets during bootstrap.
- Idempotency note: module uses lifecycle create_before_destroy for nodepools to avoid downtime on scaling operations. But major k8s version upgrades require manual cordon/drain policies configured.

7) Preflight checklist (must pass before provisioning)
- Confirm rack power/cooling specs (per-node 450W sustained).
- Provide network ACLs and route tables; validate MTU and jumbo frames for NVMe performance.
- Confirm HSM API endpoints and test key wrap/unwrap with Redwood operator account.
- Approve required IP ranges for outbound control-plane traffic or setup private link.
- Agree on monitoring retention and what logs are flagged as PHI.

8) Upgrade plan (Minor patch -> Major model/runtime upgrade)
- Minor patch (runtime patch, minor k8s patch): rolling update, 10% concurrency drain, smoke test on sample prompt set, monitor p95 and error rate for 60m. Auto rollback if error rate >3x baseline or p95 regresses >50%.
- Model variant swap (weight/quant change): use canary route (5% traffic) to new variant for 30m with synthetic prompt set and real traffic mirroring. If no regressions -> ramp 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 15m intervals.
- Major upgrade (major k8s or kernel-level infra change): schedule maintenance window (2–4 hours), perform blue/green where possible. Provision parallel k8s cluster (green) with new runtime, run full e2e evals and replayed traffic. Switch RG-level routing with DNS TTL 60s and monitor for 2h.

9) Rollback procedures
- Node-level failure during upgrade: cordon + drain then trigger new node creation using previous AMI/OS/image version.
- Model rollback: switch routing back to previous model variant via routing-policy rollback (instant) and scale down new replicas.
- Control-plane incompatibility: have runbook to switch control-plane to fallback endpoint (pre-created) and rotate API keys.

10) Monitoring, metrics and SLOs
- Required metrics to expose: token-pps, requests/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, gpu_util, kv_cache_hit_rate, model_load_time, OOM_events, error_rate.
- Alerts: p95 > 2x baseline, gpu_utilation > 95% for >10m, OOM events > 1 in 24h.
- Cost telemetry: token-cost-per-second estimates and per-request cost tagging.

11) On-prem specifics (if OrthoHealth prefers rack)
- Bootstrapping: PXE or engineered jumpbox to run firmware + OS validation, then run Terraform to create k8s nodes via MAAS or Terraform provider.
- Air-gapped: container images must be provided in offline registry tarballs; sign images and validate signatures during import.
- Upgrade caveat: offline upgrades require pre-staged model weights and operator-release bundles. Plan 48–72h longer for validation.

12) Open questions / action items (assign and follow up)
- Q1: Confirm GPU SKU availability in their datacenter: A100-80GB vs A10. (owner: Diego)
- Q2: Decide on remote-state backend: customer-managed blob vs Redwood-managed. (owner: Priya)
- Q3: Which SIEM ingestion format do they require? (owner: Liam)
- Q4: Are they OK with control-plane egress or must we use private-link? Need legal signoff for outbound telemetry. (owner: Maya)
- Q5: Confirm DR strategy: warm standby in another region or single-region with snapshots. (owner: OrthoHealth infra)

13) Quick runbook snippet for first deployment (copy/paste for runbook)
- Preflight signoff checklist complete.
- Run: terraform init -backend-config=...
- terraform apply -var-file=ortho-prod.tfvars --target=module.vpc && terraform apply --auto-approve
- Wait for k8s cluster creation, then apply rwinfra/k8s bootstrap manifests: kubectl apply -f bootstrap-secrets.yaml
- Validate: curl control-plane/health, run perf microbench: tools/perf/run --tokens 1000
- If smoke pass: notify OrthoHealth, enable routing.

14) Quick cost estimate (monthly, rough)
- HW amortized + support: $45k–$70k per month depending on GPU SKU and support SLAs.
- Redwood Private license + support tier: $20k–$40k/month.
- Total ballpark: $65k–$110k/month. (Detailed pricing to be refined after SKU confirmation.)

15) Notes to self / draft comments
- Keep this doc deliberately operational. Move final proposal text to a customer-facing one-pager once assumptions are locked.
- Need template for Terraform tfvars to hand to customer: include sample network ranges, k8s version, and SSH bastion key placeholder.

Appendix: sample terraform variables snippet (for handoff)
- cluster_name = "ortho-prod-1"
- region = "az-northeurope-1"
- subnet_ids = ["/subscriptions/.../subnets/serving-1"]
- k8s_version = "1.27"
- gpu_type = "A100-80GB"
- desired_gpu_count = "6"
- kms_key_id = "/subscriptions/.../keyvault/keys/rw-keys/"

End of draft.

Unresolved: this doc intentionally leaves model-specific memory maps and exact placement (shard strategy) for runtime team to finalize - add model topology appendix after runtime confirms per-variant memory distribution.
